study.x: Market complementarity between potential liner-shipping alliance partners
study.time_horizon: Formation of the proposed vessel-sharing alliance

x_contrast.higher: More nonoverlapping markets, retaining at least one common market

study.setting: Two liner-shipping firms consider forming a vessel-sharing alliance. Both must participate voluntarily. They share at least one market. Market complementarity concerns nonoverlapping market coverage and is distinct from compatibility of operating resources.
study.task: Rate how higher market complementarity changes the likelihood that the firms establish a vessel-sharing alliance. Compare lower X (More overlapping market portfolios) with higher X (More nonoverlapping markets, retaining at least one common market). Use the same X contrast in both contexts. A positive rating means higher X is associated with more Y; a negative rating means less Y. Rate the relationship, not the overall level of Y. Do not interpret this judgment as a measured empirical coefficient.
shared_facts: The outcome is whether the potential vessel-sharing alliance forms, not the performance of an established alliance.
The lower-versus-higher market-complementarity contrast retains at least one common market and is identical across contexts.
